result_text:
Per-extension entries are now named by the bare lower-cased extension (`"java"`, `"js"`, `"xml"`). The tests of `codeanalyzer` and `reports` pass. I didn't add a test for the landscape merge of old and new spellings.

- **`SourceCodeAspectUtils.java`:** `getAspectsPerExtensions` names each aspect with the bare extension. This feeds `linesOfCodePerExtension`, `fileCountPerExtension` and `getScopesWithExtensions`.
- **`AnalysisUtils.java`:** the metric ids are unchanged (`LINES_OF_CODE_MAIN_EXT_JAVA` and the rest). I dropped the `replace("*.", "")` that used to strip the decoration. The textual summary line still prints `  *.ext: N files, …`.
- **`LandscapeAnalysisResults.java`:** a new `bareExtension` helper normalizes every name to the bare lower-case extension. It is used in `getLinesOfCodePerExtension`, so main and the merged other category produce one entry per extension whether a repository's data says `"  *.java"` or `"java"`. It is also used in the private `merge` of build/generated/other, so the same repository can't produce two entries. Each merged entry keeps one per-repository breakdown line for every repository that contributed.
- **Tests:** `CodeConfigurationTest` and `NamedSourceCodeAspectTest` now assert `"java"`, `"js"` and `"html"` instead of the decorated names.

I left the existing `.replace("*.", "")` calls in the report code alone, because they are harmless no-ops on bare names.
